text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: SERVICE private-vpc-controlplane-heartbeat-throttled for customer 'AcmeCorp' (private VPC). Severity: P1. Trigger: heartbeat drop detected across control plane nodes.

pagerduty: Alert details — https://pd.example/alerts/PD-98321. Notifying rotation: on-call ben.

Ben (oncall): ACK — I'm on it. pinging infra + cs. taking initial triage.

Ben (oncall): Quick check: Prom shows heartbeat drops for `acme-co` in the last 90s. No widespread API 503s observed yet but control plane health is degraded for this customer.

Alice (SRE): joining the thread. Any planned maintenance for AcmeCorp right now?

Carla (Infra): No maintenance. I'm checking VPC route tables, NACLs, and ENI activity for the customer's subnets — give me ~2m.

Ben (oncall): Running prometheus query:
```
redwood_private_controlplane_heartbeat_count{customer="acme-co"}[2m]
```
Shows several missed beats aligned with the alert window.

Alice (SRE): Can you `kubectl -n private-controlplane get pods -l customer=acme-co -o wide` and paste pod states? Sidecars often crash on resource pressure.

Ben (oncall): Pods snapshot:
```
acme-ctrl-0   Running   2/2   10.3.2.4   Ready
acme-ctrl-1   Running   1/2   10.3.2.5   CrashLoopBackOff (sidecar)
```
Sidecar on acme-ctrl-1 is CrashLoopBackOff; node: ip-10-3-5-8.

Carla (Infra): Node logs (dmesg) show OOM kill targeting `redwood-agent` around the same timeframe. Also high ENI attach/detach churn seen in cloud API. Could be transient host instability causing heartbeat delays.

Dmitri (CS): Notified AcmeCorp. They report agent reconnect lags and errors opening new sessions for ~2-3 minutes. They're seeing degraded admin UI controls during window.

Emily (Support): Drafting customer message: "We're investigating intermittent connectivity between your agents and our private control plane. Engineers are actively triaging; no action required from you right now." Will send once we confirm mitigation.

Ben (oncall): Temporary mitigation: I'm going to restart the sidecar and bump CPU requests/limits to avoid immediate OOM. Applying patch:
```
kubectl -n private-controlplane rollout restart deployment/acme-ctrl --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"sidecar","resources":{"limits":{"cpu":"500m"},"requests":{"cpu":"300m"}}}]}}}}'
```

Ben (oncall): Sidecar restarted on acme-ctrl-1; heartbeats recovering.

Alice (SRE): Good. Keep monitoring 15m for regressions. Also collect a tcpdump for later analysis: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/acme-ctrl.pcap` for 30s.

Carla (Infra): Collecting pcap. VPC Flow Logs show transient ICMP 'destination unreachable' messages on the customer subnet in the same window. Opening a support case with cloud provider to see if host experienced networking interrupts.

Ben (oncall): Prom metrics back to steady: `redwood_private_controlplane_heartbeat{customer="acme-co"}` normalized. No API 503 increase in frontplane. Marking incident as mitigated for now.

Alice (SRE): We'll keep incident open for root cause. If cloud provider confirms host/kernel issue we should rotate underlying nodes and schedule a maintenance window. Assigning follow-up incident INF-4231.

Dmitri (CS): AcmeCorp reports impact limited to admin console control plane UX for ~3 minutes, no data loss. They're OK with maintenance if we need it.

Ben (oncall): Handoff to Alice for postmortem and follow-up. I'll update PagerDuty: keep assigned? Suggest leaving open until we get cloud provider RCA.

Alice (SRE): Taking owner of the follow-up. Updating PD to keep incident open for RC investigation and recording timeline. Thanks everyone — please add any additional logs to INF-4231.

incident-bot: Note — Ben acknowledged at 2487654350. Escalated to Alice at 2487654450. Please populate the postmortem template in INF-4231 with timeline and artifacts.
